position.summary: This week was dominated by a sharp deterioration in US-Ukraine relations after President Trump waived new Russia sanctions under the Graham Act, citing national interest, just days after signing them into law. Zelenskyy called the move wrong and accused the US of helping Russia, while Moscow hailed it as historic. Congress expressed outrage but had no quick legislative counter. The timing ahead of midterms intensified partisan fights, with Democrats using the Iran war and the sanctions waiver as campaign themes. Inside the White House, press secretary Katie Zacharia was fired after just five days amid criticism over her legal credentials, adding to a pattern of turmoil. Trump also threatened California officials with imprisonment over mail-ballot rules and rallied in Georgia and Pennsylvania as Republican midterm prospects dimmed. No Kings rallies drew voters nationwide to cast early ballots. The US budget deficit ballooned to nearly two trillion dollars, the largest in five years, while interest costs hit a record one trillion. Markets were battered by a tech-sector sell-off and credit fears, with bank stocks posting their worst weekly losing streak since 2008. A school shooting in Oregon left four dead, and US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz escalated with both sides claiming control of the waterway.

key_events.event: Trump waived new Russia sanctions and energy tariffs under the Graham Act, citing national interest, triggering a rift with Zelenskyy and outrage in Congress.
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was fired after only five days in the role amid criticism over her legal background and a botched first briefing.
The US annual budget deficit swelled to nearly two trillion dollars, the largest in five years, while federal interest costs hit a record one trillion.
US midterm campaign intensified with No Kings rallies, Trump threatening California over mail ballots, and party ads attacking each other over the Iran war and Russia sanctions.
US and Iran both claimed control of the Strait of Hormuz amid attacks on vessels, and Trump said the US may need to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain site.
A school shooting in Oregon left four people dead, including three children, with an armed father confronting the gunman.
US bank stocks posted their worst weekly losing streak since 2008 as a tech-sector sell-off and credit fears weighed on markets.
FBI agents and analysts fired for their roles in the Trump classified-files probe filed a lawsuit to get their jobs back.
The US began reviving shuttered nuclear plants to meet growing electricity demand and power AI data centers, while Anthropic's Clark told policymakers AI could vastly boost US GDP.

No Kings rallies, Trump's threats against California ballot rules, and heated midterm Senate debates show elections were the central domestic focus.

velocity.summary: Between the two reports the U.S. situation broadened and sharpened rather than calmed. The Iran-Hormuz crisis, previously in a diplomatic stalemate over a seven-day reopening plan, escalated to both sides claiming control of the waterway, attacks on shipping, and a presidential threat to strike the Pickaxe Mountain site. A major new rupture appeared: Trump waived freshly signed Russia sanctions under the Graham Act, splitting Washington from Kyiv and provoking congressional outrage just ahead of the midterms. Domestic economic stress deepened, with the annual deficit hitting nearly two trillion dollars, record interest costs, and bank stocks posting their worst weekly losing streak since 2008. White House turmoil accelerated with the press secretary fired after five days, while the midterm fight intensified around No Kings rallies, a California mail-ballot showdown, and party ads weaponizing both Iran and Russia. Themes from the prior report such as the Trump-Xi summit, the Iraq withdrawal, the northeast storm, and the Burundi deportation faded from view. The pace of change is brisk: several high-importance items appeared for the first time within seventy-two hours, and the agenda shifted from a single foreign crisis to a multi-front domestic and diplomatic squeeze.
